column4: thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "Write H=R^x and N=Rad_MF(H)." Naming only. mfHomKernel is the printed N, defined as the intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms to MF groups.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "Ara, Goodearl, and Pardo show that kappa is surjective with kernel [H,H] [AGP, Theorem 2.4]." PROVED, not cited, for the canonical kappa : R^x -> K_1(R) of KOne/AlgebraicKOne.lean. agpUnitKappaResidue is the same statement with the clause commutator <= ker kappa removed, that clause being free from Whitehead's lemma; it was declared in MFQuotientUnitsKappaResidue.lean and left undischarged until e3349b77d. The carrier is stated at the canonical kappa the paragraph before the theorem defines; the abstract-target reading is the second declaration.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "A countable abelian group A is MF: C*_max(A) is commutative and separable, hence residually finite-dimensional and MF [BK], and Lemma prop:mf-residual-calculus applies." Carried unconditionally by a DIFFERENT argument from the printed one: LEF and residual finiteness of finitely generated abelian groups, via isOperatorMF_of_commGroup_countable. Nothing is quoted, so Brown-Kirchberg is not an input. Same conclusion.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "So kappa is a homomorphism to an MF group, and N <= ker kappa." The intersection of the kernels of all homomorphisms to MF groups is contained in the kernel of any one of them.
thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "For the converse we use Theorem thm:full-defect-ring in the following form." Announces the form; the form itself is the next sentence.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "Every nonzero idempotent e of R is infinite [AGP, Proposition 1.5], so eRe contains s,t with ts=e!=st, and eRe is simple, so e-st generates eRe as a two-sided ideal; hence every homomorphism from EL_m(eRe), m>=2, to an MF group is trivial." AGP Proposition 1.5 is PROVED (isInfiniteIdempotent_of_ne_zero), not cited. The consumed final clause is carried for an arbitrary countable ring with a one-sided inverse pair whose complementary idempotent is full, which is what the earlier clauses say of eRe. Unconditional as of e3349b77d: thm:full-defect-ring in rank-two form is FullDefectRingEJZUnconditional.manuscriptFullComplementaryIdempotentsRankTwoAllCharacteristics.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof, the display eq:corner-units and its justification: "since these units form the image of EL_m(eRe) under a homomorphism to H." The printed justification is the whole content and it is general: the image of a group with no nontrivial homomorphism to an MF group lies in the intersection of all their kernels (range_le_mfHomKernel). Neither the corner ring eRe nor theta is constructed. Carrier unconditional as of e3349b77d.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "We use two facts from the proof of [AGP, Theorem 2.4], which rest on [AGP, Proposition 1.5 and Corollary 1.7] and on the elementary reduction of Menal and Moncasi." Provenance sentence. manuscriptAGPInputs is the closed proposition recording that every one of the six named Ara-Goodearl-Pardo propositions of this proof is a theorem on the tree rather than an assumption, so the attribution is now historical rather than a dependency.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof, quoted fact (b): "For a nonzero idempotent e and n>=2 there are an idempotent f<e equivalent to e and orthogonal idempotents r_2,...,r_n <= e-f, each equivalent to 1, such that, with r_1=1-e+f and P=r_1+...+r_n, some ring isomorphism theta : M_n(R) -> PRP sends diag(v,1,...,1) to (1-e)v(1-e)+f+r_2+...+r_n for every unit v=e+(1-e)v(1-e)." The consumed conclusion is PROVED, not cited; theta is built as a matrix-corner homomorphism into R^x.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "Let u in ker kappa and write u=gvh as in (a)." Carrier is unconditional as of e3349b77d and holds for EVERY unit, not only for one in ker kappa; it took AGPMenalMoncasiReduction as a binder before.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "The elementary matrices with i,j <= m-1 form EL_{m-1}(T) inside (1-e_m)R(1-e_m) = M_{m-1}(T), so they lie in N by eq:corner-units." The consumed content is eq:corner-units applied to the corner; the corner ring is not constructed, as the corner-unit subgroup quantifies over all countable rings with the relevant one-sided pair.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "Hence u = v modulo N, and kappa(v)=kappa(u)=0 because N <= ker kappa." u and v differ by a corner unit, corner units lie in N, and N <= ker kappa, so kappa cannot tell them apart.
thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "So let v=e+(1-e)v(1-e) with e!=0 and kappa(v)=0." Introduces the hypotheses of fact (b); they are the binders of agpStepOne.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "With theta and P as in (b), v=1-P+theta(diag(v,1,...,1)), which lies in N by eq:corner-units." Carried as the conclusion v in cornerUnitSubgroup R, which with eq:corner-units gives v in N. theta and P are internal to the proof rather than named objects of the statement.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof, final sentence: "Hence ker kappa <= N." With the sentence N <= ker kappa this is N = ker kappa = [H,H], which with the rank reduction is the theorem. Carrier unconditional as of e3349b77d; it took four literature-package binders before.

thm:mf-quotient-units statement, clause 1: "Then every homomorphism from GL_n(R) to an MF group factors uniquely through the canonical map GL_n(R) -> K_1(R), and K_1(R), a countable abelian group, is MF." manuscriptCanonicalKOne carries the unique factorization through the canonical matrixKappa at every rank n >= 1 together with IsOperatorMF (AlgebraicKOne R); manuscriptMFQuotientUnitsKOne is the rank-one form with all four printed clauses.

thm:mf-quotient-units statement, clause 2: "Equivalently, Rad_MF(GL_n(R))=[GL_n(R),GL_n(R)] and GL_n(R)/Rad_MF(GL_n(R)) = K_1(R)." Both displays at every rank n >= 1, with the quotient named K_1(R) on the nose and with NO Morita input: the identification runs through the stable group.

cor:leavitt-mf-quotient statement: "Then H = GL_d(R), and under this identification Rad_MF(H)=[H,H]=EL_d(R) and H/EL_d(R) = K_1(R) = k^x/(k^x)^{d-1}." Everything up to and including H/EL_d(R) = K_1(R) is proved, at every countable field and every d >= 2. PARTIAL only for the final isomorphism K_1(R) = k^x/(k^x)^{d-1}, which is the open half of the Khanh-Thanh citation, tracked as LeavittKOneFormula.PrintedLeavittKOneFormula (lane o-leavitt-k1). The H/EL_d(R) = K_1(R) display was previously uncarried and is new in this lane.

cor:leavitt-mf-quotient proof: "The maps x -> (t_1 x,...,t_d x) and (y_1,...,y_d) -> sum_i s_i y_i are mutually inverse isomorphisms of right R-modules between R and R^d, so R = M_d(R) and H = GL_d(R)." The consumed conclusion H = GL_d(R) is carried at every field and every d >= 2; the two displayed formulas are pinned on the nose at d=2 by manuscriptSentence_rightModuleSelfSimilarity, which exhibits them as a bundled right-module LinearEquiv.

cor:leavitt-mf-quotient proof: "Theorem thm:mf-quotient-units identifies the radical with [H,H] and the quotient with K_1(R)." BOTH clauses, applied to R=L_k(1,d) at rank d, with nothing assumed. New in this lane: the quotient clause had no carrier before, because LeavittMFQuotientGeneral.lean states that the identification of the quotient with K_1(R) is not carried. It is now, from MFQuotientCanonicalKOne.manuscriptMFQuotientUnitsKOneAtBaseRing plus AryLeavitt.isPurelyInfiniteSimpleRing.

cor:leavitt-mf-quotient proof: "Khanh-Thanh show that GL_d(R)=EL_d(R)D_d(k), where D_d(k) is the abelian group of diagonal matrices with entries in k^x, which normalizes EL_d(R), and that K_1(R) = k^x/(k^x)^{d-1}." The half the printed chain consumes, [GL_d(R),GL_d(R)] <= EL_d(R), is PROVED rather than cited: pure infiniteness gives single-sandwich division, Gaussian elimination puts every invertible matrix in the form E.diag.F, and Whitehead's identity kills the commutators of the diagonal image. PARTIAL for the two clauses not asserted: the decomposition GL_d(R)=EL_d(R)D_d(k) itself (lane o-leavitt-ge) and K_1(R) = k^x/(k^x)^{d-1} (lane o-leavitt-k1).

cor:leavitt-mf-quotient proof: "So [H,H] <= EL_d(R), while EL_d(R) <= [H,H] because every homomorphism from EL_d(R) to an MF group is trivial (Theorem thm:full-defect-ring)." All three clauses: both inclusions and the printed reason for the second one, which is where thm:full-defect-ring enters. Unconditional at every countable field and every d >= 2.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "for distinct i,j <= m-1, e_im(x)=[e_ij(1),e_jm(x)], e_mj(x)=[e_mi(x),e_ij(1)] are products of an element of EL_{m-1}(T) and a conjugate of its inverse, so they lie in the normal subgroup N as well." UPGRADED from partial. Both printed identities AND the printed conclusion are carried. The identities are instances of the general elementary commutator relation elementaryUnit_commutator; the conclusion is the printed reason read literally, that a normal subgroup containing ONE of the two factors contains the commutator, since [A,B]=A(B A^-1 B^-1) when A is in N and [A,B]=(A B A^-1)B^-1 when B is. The two displays use opposite factors, so both cases are needed and both are proved. Stated over an arbitrary ring and finite index type rather than inside the twisted m x m matrix ring: the twisting constrains which x may appear in the last row and column, while the identity and the membership hold for every x, so the general statement CONTAINS the twisted one. steinbergCommutatorMemNormal is the ring-level form that applies inside the twisted ring verbatim, with 1 read as the printed diag(1_T,...,1_T,f) and the two square-zero matrix units as a and b.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof: "By the definition of K_1, diag(v,1,...,1) in EL_n(R) for some n >= 2." UPGRADED from partial: the printed EL_n(R) spelling at printed rank n >= 2 is now proved. Previously the tree had only KappaProof.exists_diagonal_mem_commutator, which lands in the COMMUTATOR subgroup and only at some rank n > 0. Two steps closed the gap: the rank is pushed to max n 2 by glStab along n <= max n 2 with glStab_one_eq_diagAt at both ends (glStab_diagAt), and at rank at least two the two subgroups coincide by MFQuotientMatrices.mfHomKernel_matrixUnits_eq. manuscriptSentence_diagInElementaryAndCommutator records both readings at the same rank.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof, sentence 1: "The ring M_n(R) is again countable, purely infinite, and simple [AGP, Corollary 1.7], and K_1(M_n(R)) = K_1(R) by Morita invariance, so it suffices to treat n=1." UPGRADED from partial (landed ace5ecf8d). All three clauses now carried: AGP Corollary 1.7 is agpMatrixReduction, countability of a matrix ring over a countable ring is automatic, and the Morita isomorphism is MFQuotientUnitsKOne.moritaKOne, proved in KOne/MoritaKOne.lean for an arbitrary unital ring and every n >= 1. Note for provenance: nothing downstream ever waited on Morita. MFQuotientCanonicalKOne.manuscriptMFQuotientUnitsKOneAtBaseRing already reached the printed conclusion at K_1(R) through the rank-n map matrixKappa rather than through K_1(M_n(R)), and moritaKOneEquiv_matrixKappa proves the two routes agree. What was missing was the printed SENTENCE, never the printed THEOREM.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof, quoted fact (a), first sentence: "There are orthogonal idempotents e_1,...,e_m with sum 1, m>=4, such that e_1,...,e_{m-1} are pairwise equivalent and e_m is equivalent to an idempotent f <= e_1." Now carried LITERALLY by printedItemA, whose existential produces exactly this decomposition for every purely infinite simple ring and every m >= 4, audit-closed. Stronger than a formality: f is a genuine copy of the last block inside e_1, not the degenerate choice f = e_1 that would satisfy the printed hypothesis while collapsing the twisting the sentence is about. agpMenalMoncasiReduction and unit_reduces_to_supported remain listed because they are what the rest of the printed proof actually consumes, by a two-index Peirce route that does not build the m-block decomposition.

thm:mf-quotient-units proof, quoted fact (a), second sentence: "Then R is the ring of m x m matrices over T=e_1Re_1, with identity diag(1_T,...,1_T,f), whose last column has entries in Tf and whose last row has entries in fT, and every unit u of R factors as u=gvh with g and h products of elementary matrices e_ij(x) of this matrix ring and v=e_1+(1-e_1)v(1-e_1)." BOTH halves now carried, and my earlier partial note is WITHDRAWN as stale. Matrix identification: PeirceTwistedMatrixRing builds the ring as the corner of M_m(T) at the printed diagonal matrix, so the identity is the corner unit by construction, and mem_twistedCorner_iff restates the corner's defining equations in the printed Tf / fT form. Factorization: printedItemAShape proves the u=gvh clause at EVERY decomposition meeting item (a)'s hypotheses. printedItemA conjoins the whole sentence and is audit-closed.
